Affiliation:: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Oklahoma, Tulsa, OK 74135, USA
Data & Platforms: University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center (OUHSC) Dataset
Application Areas: Privacy-Preserving Medical Imaging and Healthcare Collaboration
Trustworthy and Interpretable Deep Learning Architectures
Digital Forensics and Synthetic Media Security
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Cryptographic Verification of Distributed Learning: Utilizing Zero-Knowledge Proofs and multivariate polynomial proxy models to ensure gradient integrity and privacy in decentralized federated learning environments without compromising model performance.

Information-Theoretic Uncertainty Quantification: Leveraging entropy-adjusted dynamic routing and information-theoretic metrics to enhance the robustness and interpretability of capsule networks, enabling reliable part-whole hierarchy learning under noisy conditions.

Generative Model Forensics and Mitigation: Conducting systematic analyses of deepfake evolution across GANs and diffusion models to develop cross-modal detection frameworks that address the challenges of synthetic media misinformation and regulatory compliance.

Weakly Supervised Anomaly Detection in Medical Imaging: Applying denoising diffusion probabilistic models and U-Net architectures to detect pancreatic tumors and medical anomalies with limited labeled data, bridging the gap between generative AI and clinical diagnostic utility.
Summary Description: Samuel Cheng specializes in trustworthy, privacy-preserving AI, integrating medical image analysis, cryptographic security, and digital forensics. He advances decentralized federated learning through ProxyZKP, employing zero-knowledge proofs for gradient verification, and enhances capsule networks via entropy-adjusted dynamic routing for interpretable uncertainty quantification. His work applies denoising diffusion models to weakly supervised medical anomaly detection, specifically pancreatic tumor segmentation. Concurrently, he addresses synthetic media threats by analyzing deepfake evolution across GANs and diffusion platforms to build robust, cross-modal detection systems. Cheng’s research bridges generative AI, cryptographic integrity, and information-theoretic robustness, aiming to deploy secure, ethical, and clinically impactful AI solutions.
